> Actually in standard Civ V:
> - DP between A and B.
> - If A is attacked by C, B is called to war against C.
> - If A attacks C, no one is called.
> - But if A attacks B, and B has a DP with C, C is called against A.
>
> So:
> - I (China) attack Brazil.
> - Brazil has DP with Indonesia. Indonesia is called against me.
> - I have DP with Portugal. But I was the attacker, not the defender. So Portugal is NOT called.
> - However, if Indonesia now attacks me (because of their DP with Brazil), am I considered "attacked"? The game usually considers this as Indonesia honoring their DP, and it might trigger my DP with Portugal. But in practice, Civ V handles DP chains weirdly.
